acceptanceCriteria: Spike defines the input shapes (host transcript formats), the friction classes it detects, and the secret-screen and byte bounds.
If pursued: a skill or read-only command emits ticket proposals with transcript citations and a duplicate check against existing tickets, and never mutates the store itself.
Evaluation on a small set of retained real transcripts reports precision of the proposals against owner judgment.
body: Source: GitHub trending review 2026-10-16 (idea only; nothing was adopted or measured). Prior art: obra/superpowers ships a 'figure out what went wrong' skill that reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report. The owner's standing instruction asks agents to file friction, bugs and missing capabilities automatically, yet filing depends on the agent noticing at the time. A post-mortem pass over a finished Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode transcript could propose deduplicated agent-memory tickets: Corvint fallbacks such as dogfood-event-deadline, refused Tasks mutations, repeated failed commands, and packet misses that the agent then grepped for. Each proposal carries transcript line citations and is secret-screened. Proposals only; filing stays an explicit Tasks mutation. Transcripts are untrusted model and host output, per V1-0712.
title: Idea: transcript post-mortem that turns a misbehaving agent session into evidence-cited tickets
